conviction_note: Nothing decisive found. The setup leans slightly up: a full-year OP plan of 47.0bn sits 6% under IFIS consensus (50.2bn), so the half-year plan implies H2 OP down 16% YoY. Q3 laps a 7.4%-margin Q3 2025 with the yen weaker YoY. Against that, Shimano held its plan at the last two Q3 prints and both were sold (-4.3%, -7.4% on the cadence history). The headwinds the company named (oil, Asian-currency costs, waiting for a new road groupset) and a Q3 yen rebound below OP are all public. So p_up is 53 on a 4.5% scale (+0.27). The findings sum to +0.45 by a separate measure, and both are small because the most likely outcome is another held plan that the street already looks through.
bar: IFIS consensus FY2026 (Dec) OP 50,232m / ordinary 60,850m as of 2026-10-26 (https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/reportAnalyst?bcode=7309; ordinary also confirmed at https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/7309_20261026_cons_20261026_224635_22), against the company plan of OP 47,000m / ordinary 56,000m (held/raised 2026-07-28). The pre-Q2 Q3 consensus was OP 10,667m (https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/7309_20260728_act_20260728_153015_3), and no post-Q2 Q3 quarter consensus was found. print_vs_bar is OP versus that consensus path, an estimate.
positioning_check: JPX disclosed shorts are 0.58% of shares (one seller), down 0.02pt into the print (baseline, as of 2026-10-26, https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html). 信用倍率 is 0.56 (kabutan page 2026-10-27), so margin shorts outnumber margin longs, which is mild squeeze fuel. Rating consensus is 3.0 neutral across 8 analysts with a TP consensus of 19,018 against spot 18,690, and a US broker started at Equal-Weight with TP 18,000 on 10/23 (https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/7309_20261023_rep_20261026_140512_21). Japan has no skew. The baseline priced_lean is +0.29 and run_up_20d is +4.41.

findings.finding: At Q2 Shimano kept its full-year OP plan at 47.0bn even though H1 OP beat its own H1 plan by 13.5% (27.2bn vs 24.0bn). The plan therefore implies H2 OP of 19.75bn (-16% YoY), against IFIS consensus of 50.2bn, which needs H2 of about 23.0bn. Shimano has not revised at its last two Q3 prints (no revision notice on 2024-10-29 or 2025-10-28), then beat its FY2025 plan by 12% (46.0bn to 51.7bn). So a hold is the base case and is already discounted by the street, and a raise toward consensus is the upside tail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-28: Q3 held the plan, Q3 OP about 1.5bn under the market, stock -7.4% (estimated-cadence history; Fisco: https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=7309&b=n202510290537). 2024-10-29: held, -4.3%. 2026-07-28: held the OP plan but raised sales and ordinary, with a Q2 OP beat of about 3bn, stock +10.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus already sits about 3bn above the plan and TP consensus is barely above spot, so the street prices roughly a held plan plus a later beat, not a raise at this print. If a raise were expected, the 4-week consensus drift would be larger (60,577 to 60,850 ordinary is flat) and the stock would not sit 13% under its 7/30 high of 21,530.
findings.independence: The plan numbers come from the Q2 tanshin itself (https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/73090/140120260727599816.pdf). The irbank disclosure list shows no Q3 revision notice in 2024 or 2025 (https://irbank.net/7309/ir). Consensus is a different source (kabuyoho).

findings.finding: Q3 laps a depressed base: Q3 2025 OP was 8,442m on a 7.4% margin, after Q2 2026 already printed +40.6% YoY. The yen averaged weaker in Q3 2026 than in Q3 2025 (about 157-162 against about 147), which lifts sales translation. Giant, a direct customer, reported September 2026 revenue +2.9% YoY with its own-brand China sales +26% on MTB/e-bike, Europe flat and the US down. That fits Shimano's H1 commentary on China commuter MTB recovering.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A Q2 2026 quarter OP beat of about 3bn bought +10.4%. A Q1 2026 miss (OP -35.6% YoY) sold -5.2%. A Q3 2025 miss of about 1.5bn sold -7.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: analysts lifted ordinary consensus after Q2. No post-Q2 Q3 quarter consensus is visible, and the pre-Q2 figure (OP 10.7bn) predates the Q2 beat. Giant's 9M revenue is still -5% YoY, so the bike recovery reads as uneven rather than strong, which leaves the quarter open in both directions.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 base and margin: https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=7309. Yen levels: Sep 30 2026 at 156.9 (https://www.oanda.jp/lab-education/?p=129162) and Jun 30 2026 at 162.25 (https://finance.matsui.co.jp/news/622980/index). These are different sources from the Giant figure.

findings.finding: The yen strengthened over the quarter, from about 162.25 on June 30 to about 156.9 on Sept 30 2026. That points to a foreign-currency valuation loss below operating income in Q3, against a 1.8bn H1 FX gain, while ordinary consensus (60.85bn) needs about 25.5bn of H2 ordinary profit. Shimano's sensitivity has varied widely (H1 2025: 21.7bn loss on about an 8% yen move; H1 2026: only 1.8bn gain on about 3%), so the size is unknown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-07-29: an H1 hit mainly from a 21.7bn FX loss came with a -23.3% reaction (cadence history), alongside other items. Holders usually look through Shimano's FX valuation line.
findings.why_not_priced: The yen path is public, but the ordinary consensus has drifted up (+0.7% week on week) rather than down, which suggests analysts have not marked an FX valuation loss into Q3. It sits below OP and has no path to the OP guide, hence small.

findings.finding: Alpecin raced a prototype 13-speed Dura-Ace R9300 at the 2026 Vuelta (Aug-Sep), while the current groupset dates from 2021. That points to high-end road buyers holding off before a launch, a drag on H2 bicycle-component sales that supports the company's conservative H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a groupset cycle in the baseline history. Bike-segment OP fell 15.1% YoY in H1 2026 while fishing rose.
findings.source_date: 2026-09 (Vuelta 2026; page date not confirmed in the document)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: a race sighting is public and the stock fell from about 19.9k (8/31) to 18.2k (9/18) during the Vuelta. What could be new is management saying so in the Q3 outlook. It is a road-only proxy, net of MTB, e-bike and fishing (fishing H1 +17%).
findings.independence: Shimano's Q2 tanshin says China road demand stayed subdued (https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/73090/140120260727599816.pdf). An unsourced broker snippet on traders.co.jp says the same (rejected for no date).

findings.finding: Crude briefly traded above $100 on 2026-10-19. Shimano named the Middle-East oil spike and Asian-currency strength as the reasons it held OP at 47bn in July, so the headwind it cited has intensified into the print. That makes a held plan more likely than a raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: the OP plan was held on these stated headwinds and the stock still rose 10.4% on the quarter beat.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-19 (INPEX headline on the traders.co.jp page: NY crude briefly above $100)
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, because the oil price is public. It is filed only because it lowers the odds of finding 1's upside tail. Macro-to-company transmission, so it is small.
findings.independence: The company's own statement of the oil headwind is in the Q2 tanshin, section (3) (https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/73090/140120260727599816.pdf).

findings.finding: The ¥50bn buyback set on 2026-02-10 (to 2027-01-31) had used ¥41.4bn (2.37m of 2.95m shares) by 9/30, at about ¥4.2bn a month, so it runs out around November. In 2025 the program's completion was announced on the Q3 day, and the next program came only with the February full-year results. A new program at this print is not the base case, and market support of about 5% of daily turnover is ending soon.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-28: completion announced with Q3, no new program, -7.4%, driven mainly by the quarter. 2024-10-29: a buyback method was added at Q3, -4.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Neutral by construction: upside if an additional program is set (there was a shareholder proposal at the March AGM, per the 2026-02-27 board-opinion notice), but the base rate at Q3 is 0 of 2.
findings.independence: The disclosure pattern comes from the irbank list (https://irbank.net/7309/ir).

findings.finding: Margin positioning is short-heavy (信用倍率 0.56) with disclosed shorts small and edging down (0.60% to 0.58%). Sell-side sentiment is lukewarm (8 analysts, rating 3.0, TP consensus 19,018; MS-type Equal-Weight TP 18,000 started 10/23), so the bar for a positive surprise in the reaction is low.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July 2026 positive surprise ran +10.4% over three up days, consistent with short covering.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly in the baseline's priced_lean (+0.29). Filed small because it only amplifies a positive surprise and does not create one.
findings.independence: The margin ratio is on the kabutan quote header (https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=7309). The short register is JPX via the baseline.

outside_window.finding: Launch of the next-generation Dura-Ace R9300 groupset, whose timing would set 2027 road sell-in. It is unannounced, with rumours pointing to late 2026 or 2027.
Completion of the ¥50bn buyback (¥8.6bn left at 9/30) and any new program, most likely with the FY results in February, as in 2025.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: possible but not the base case (Shimano held at Q3 in 2024 and 2025). The plan sits 6% under consensus OP, so a raise is upside and a hold is the habit. Returns: the dividend of 363 was already set, and a new buyback is unlikely with ¥8.6bn of the current program left. New-year guide: none (Q3 of a December year). Quarter: 9M OP progress against the 47bn plan was 79.5% at Q3 2025. A Q3 2026 OP of about 11-12bn would put progress at about 81-83%, so the progress rate does not move the bar on its own.

baseline_tension: Roughly in line with the baseline: a small positive lean (+0.29 priced_lean, +4.4% run-up, short-heavy margin). I looked for the strongest positive the release could carry: a raise of the 47bn OP plan toward the 50.2bn consensus, or a new buyback. Raises at Q3 have a 0/2 base rate in 2024-25, and the buyback still has ¥8.6bn left, so neither is the base case. The negatives (yen rebound below OP, oil, a road groupset pause) are public series and small. Net, close to a non-result.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative on a public series goes toward 50): the three negatives rest on public macro and industry series (yen path, oil price, a race sighting). FX one-off went from -0.2 to -0.15, Dura-Ace from -0.3 to -0.2, oil from -0.2 to -0.1.
Rule 2 (check the sign): I looked for the positives (a held or raised plan, a buyback, a dividend) and recorded them in baseline_tension. The positive findings are unchanged.
p_up moved from 52 to 53 because the negatives' weight fell. abs_move_pct is unchanged at 4.5.
